# Newsletter charter

The newsletter made its readers one promise at signup, and every cycle-level
decision inherits it: findings they can check, in minutes they can spare, at a
cadence that respects their inbox.

The cadence is fixed and honest. An issue ships when the cycle has findings worth a
reader's minutes; a thin cycle ships a short issue rather than a padded one, and a
genuinely empty cycle skips with a one-line note rather than manufacturing content.
Skipping honestly costs less trust than shipping filler.

The subject line is the strongest finding stated plainly. No curiosity gaps, no
urgency theater, no "you won't believe" mechanics — the reader opens the issue to
get the finding's evidence, not to discover what the finding was.

Reader data is used for exactly one thing: sending the newsletter. No engagement
scoring is shared beyond the function, no individual reading behavior is discussed
in any meeting, and the unsubscribe path works in one click with no exit survey in
the way.

Sponsorships and placements do not exist in this newsletter. The day that changes
is the day the charter is rewritten in public, in the newsletter itself, before the
first placed item appears.

## Archive parity

Every issue lands in the public archive the day it sends, so the newsletter is never
a gated version of the company's writing. Subscribers get findings first by hours,
not exclusively — the charter trades artificial scarcity for durable trust.
